title: Yusuf's Dream Was Already Solved — by One Word Ending, Before Anyone Interpreted It
excerpt: In the first scene of Surah Yusuf, the boy describes eleven stars, the sun, and the moon 'prostrating' — but he refers to them with the pronoun and plural ending Arabic reserves for rational, conscious beings, quietly promoting the stars to people before anyone mentions his family. Ninety-six verses later the surah closes the ring: his family fall in prostration (same root, s-j-d) and Yusuf declares 'this is the meaning of my dream.' Al-Jalalayn names the grammar move directly.
seo_title: The Grammar in Yusuf 12:4 That Already Interpreted His Dream
seo_description: In Quran 12:4 Yusuf calls the prostrating stars 'them' with the rational-being grammar (hum, sajidin) — al-Jalalayn ties it to the act of prostration. The surah closes the ring at 12:100 (same root s-j-d). A corpus-verified reading of grammar and ring composition in Surah Yusuf.
